newsitem.title: UK: Sears' woes revive break-up speculation.
newsitem.headline: Sears' woes revive break-up speculation.

text.p: Breaking up is hard to do but may prove the most attractive option for British retailer Sears Plc, whose shares and profits are in the doldrums despite efforts to shake-up its far-flung retail empire, analysts said on Wednesday.

Results later this month are not likely to cheer long-suffering shareholders, with profits set to be some 20 percent down on last year's 100 million pounds ($162.6 million) and weak current trading unlikely to suggest things are on the up.

Sears' ailing British Shoe Corporation has been struggling in a tough footwear market, and childrenswear chain Adams' has been hit by a shift away from traditional kidswear to shops specialising in trendy branded fashion.

Even star performer Selfridges, the London department store, will not do as well because of disruption caused by refurbishment and a drop in tourist spending because of the strong pound, analysts said.
"It's difficult to see anything in the way of recovery coming through," said one retail analyst.

The sense that things are still getting worse plus impatience with Sears' on-again-off again attempts to sell Freemans mail order has prompted renewed speculation about a break-up and revived talk that chief executive Liam Strong's days may be numbered.
The logic is that British Shoe and other poor performers could be sold off, Selfridges floated, leaving womenswear stores -- including Wallis and Warehouse, as a more manageable business.
Break-up valuation estimates range from 115 pence down to 95 pence a share. But some analysts remain sceptical that it will happen because of difficulties valuing British Shoe.

Break-up rumours included speculation that German mail order group Otto Versand AG might mount a takeover to get its hands on Sears' home shopping business Freemans, which Sears is trying to sell to Littlewoods.
Privately-held Otto has denied recent press reports it was considering break-up bid, saying it had "no interest" in Sears or Freemans.

Retail analysts said they believed a couple of U.S. financial institutions were looking at a break-up bid, which would expose the underperforming businesses like British Shoe and unlock the value in highly profitable Selfridges. But they said it was more likely Sears would eventually perform the surgery itself.
"A break-up bid for Sears has been mooted for years, but it's never happened," said one analyst.

Sears' top management led-by Strong has been resistant to pulling the group apart. But with the shares languishing near their lowest for a year at 74 pence, analysts say institutional shareholders are pressing for change.
"A restructuring is attractive to shareholders," said another retail analyst, who estimated Selfridges was worth some 550 to 600 million pounds.
The key question is how to value British Shoe, which most analysts factor in at zero, but some see as a sizeable negative.

Strong has been able to buy time by promising investors a 410 million pound payout linked to the sale of Freemans. But this could be delayed now the deal is being investigated by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

There are also doubts Sears can get Littlewoods to pay its original 395 million pound price tag on Freemans after Sears tried and failed to sell the business to rival mail order firm N.Brown Group Plc.($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
